title: Banjo and piano roles; the drummer
summary: She and banjoist Marrero played the same chords; she would play four-four if he were out. She recalls the drummer.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When you were playing with those early bands, like, say, the Celestine band with John Marrera, what did the banjo and the piano play together? I mean, did you both play the same chords all the while, or did you play on any different beats?
I think we played the same chords. We had to, in order to have the harmony right.
Yeah, I mean, did you both play fourth of measure, or...?

Well, he was a solo man a lot. He would play... I imagine he would play four, but of course he picked a lot. Picked beautifully, and when he would take a solo, he would begin picking. Then I would take the... the compliment. But I think... I can't recall too clearly, but I think he was a sort of four-four.
In other words, if you had to do a job where, say, John Marrera was sick, and there couldn't get anybody else, would you play differently than...
Oh, I would have to play four-four in order to give the beat along with the drum.
Yeah. Who was my drum with you then? You didn't have that, do you remember? Gosh.
I think it was Chinese. I think it was Chinese. It's been quite a long while, I guess I remember.
Did you hear him play when he came back, Chinese?
No, I didn't hear him when he came back.
Tell me, it was a very fast drummer.
He was very good at that time, yes.
